subject.title: Discord compaction still fails with provider_error_4xx after #90496 closure on 2026.6.5

question: When Codex-native compaction for a Discord channel fails with HTTP 403/provider_error_4xx, should OpenClaw rotate or preserve the channel session, surface an auth/provider-specific recovery action, or leave the lane failed until manual intervention?
rationale: Current source shows the failure boundary but not a maintained product contract for automatic provider-4xx recovery, and the choice affects session continuity, message delivery, and provider/auth ownership.

options.title: Define provider-4xx recovery policy
options.body: Choose the recovery semantics first, then implement a bounded fix with live Discord/Codex proof and regression coverage for the chosen path.

options.title: Fold into timeout work
options.body: Treat the open timeout partial-progress PR as the owner, accepting that provider-403 Discord recovery remains unproven unless that PR expands scope.

options.title: Document manual recovery only
options.body: Close as provider/auth support and require users to use /new or manual reconfiguration when this failure occurs.

recommendation.title: Define provider-4xx recovery policy
recommendation.body: Choose the recovery semantics first, then implement a bounded fix with live Discord/Codex proof and regression coverage for the chosen path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged follow-up is the closest overlapping ownership signal for Codex compaction, Discord session recovery, and stale provider metadata behavior.
